content:
The 2026 World Gymnastics Championships in Rotterdam ended with a changing of the guard. China won the women's team title with 165.764 points, edging the United States by just 0.233 to end a 15-year American reign that spanned seven straight world team titles. Japan took bronze with 164.063.

The Americans led at the halfway mark and won the uneven bars rotation, but the balance beam proved decisive. Dulcy Caylor fell on her dismount while China's Zhang Qingying anchored the rotation, and China held on through the final rotation. The silver still secured the United States a berth at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics as one of the top three teams, along with China and Japan.

Skye Blakely gave the United States its brightest moment of the championships. The University of Florida junior won the women's all-around title with 55.733 points, finishing ahead of Liudmila Roshchina of the neutral WG2 team (55.199) and China's Ke Qinqin (55.032). Paris Olympic uneven bars champion Kaylia Nemour of Algeria finished fourth. Blakely is the ninth American woman to win the world all-around title and the first gymnast to win it in the same calendar year she competed in NCAA gymnastics.

Blakely led all women at the championships with four medals: gold in the all-around, silver in the team competition, and bronze on vault and uneven bars. She was the only woman to qualify for four individual event finals.

In the apparatus finals, Rebeca Andrade of Brazil won vault gold with 14.466, with American Claire Pease taking silver and Blakely bronze. Nemour defended her world title on uneven bars with 15.333 and added beam gold on a tie-break, scoring 14.566 to edge Zhang Qingying on execution. Pease closed the women's competition by winning floor gold with 13.866, with American Reese Esponda taking silver at 13.566.

On the men's side, Japan won the team title for the third consecutive time with 251.928 points, ahead of the WG2 team (250.329) and China (249.193). The United States men finished sixth with 245.161. Japan's Daiki Hashimoto won the men's all-around with 85.998.

The championships also carried a connection for Mexican fans: Simone Biles' former coach Cecile Canqueteau-Landi coached Team Mexico in Rotterdam, with Georgia freshman Jazmyn Jimenez representing Mexico, after Landi rebuilt the Georgia program and took over as head coach in April 2026.

Sources: NBC Sports; Just Women's Sports; Inside Gymnastics; Florida Gators; EssentiallySports; Longines Timing, official results.

title: Worlds 2026: Skye Blakely Wins All-Around Gold as China Ends Team USA's 15-Year Reign
